Hi Olivia — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and suggested next steps so we stay aligned with procurement and your finance team.

Call highlights:
- Primary use: inference for clinical document summarization (low single-digit RPS, bursty during EOD).
- Data: PII-lite, logs retained 30 days, audit log requirement for SOC2.
- Success criteria: sub-300ms median latency, <20% token cost uplift vs baseline, clear SLA for uptime.

Procurement & commercial signals I noted:
1) Marketplace interest: you asked about AWS Marketplace private offers vs direct PO. Sounds like Procurement prefers centralized purchase flows if billing/chargeback is easier.
2) Paper process: if legal needs a standard MSA + exhibit, we can produce a short addendum for data handling.
3) Payment rails: likely PO for enterprise purchase, but you may pilot on card or marketplace for faster onboarding.

Suggested next steps:
- Sean + Marissa: quick 30-min call with your procurement to map exact PO/paper steps (we can bring sample PO wording and marketplace SKU).
- Marissa: prepare a one-page summary comparing buy paths (AWS Private Offer, PO billing, Credit card) with pros/cons and timeline.
- Olivia: share any internal docs (RFP or procurement checklist) or the contact for procurement.

Attachments: I attached the RFP we pulled from your portal and a simple PO process diagram.

Availability: open Thu 6/15 9–11am PT or Fri 6/16 8–10am PT. Which works for procurement?

Cheers,

Hi Olivia / Procurement team — thanks for the fast response. I put together a short comparison of the three common purchase paths and the typical timing/impacts to implementation: see bullets below. I can share as a one-pager or slide depending on what helps procurement.

Short comparison (high-level):
- Direct PO (Redwood invoice to MedTech Labs):
  * Pros: flexible contract terms, direct invoicing, FTE-level support options.
  * Cons: procurement review and legal signature typically 2–4 weeks for standard terms.
  * Time-to-first-invoice: ~1–2 weeks after countersignature.
- AWS Private Offer / Marketplace:
  * Pros: aligns with centralized AWS billing, can be private offer (PO-like) or SaaS Marketplace listing; often faster approval if procurement allows marketplace spend consolidation.
  * Cons: limited custom contract language, private offers require AWS admin involvement.
  * Time-to-first-invoice: ~3–10 business days depending on AWS catalog and PO mapping.
- Card (pilot):
  * Pros: fastest (same day), minimal paperwork; good for low-risk pilots.
  * Cons: not suitable for multi-year commitments or >$50k ARR; harder for central chargeback.

SLA: we maintain operational SLAs and can provide an excerpt for legal. For pilots we recommend an initial 90-day trial with standard hosted SLA plus backups. I'll attach a redlined example MSA excerpt if helpful.

Next steps I can action this week:
- Draft one-pager comparing payment rails and expected timelines (I can send by EOD Wed).
- Share a sample MSA excerpt and our standard SOC2 attestation.
- Book a 30-min sync with Procurement to walk the one-pager and confirm required fields for the PO / AWS private offer.

If Procurement prefers, we can also run a quick pilot on card to validate latency and then convert to PO or Marketplace for production.

— Marissa
Senior Solutions Consultant | Redwood Inference
